extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedia contributors/editors who write math using LaTeX/MathJax on Wikipedia
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing LaTeX/math markup on Wikipedia pages, specifically explaining why \mbox should not be used and what to use instead. Focuses on correct commands, expected behavior in normal LaTeX vs. Wikipedia/MathJax, and line-break semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never use \mbox within Wikipedia math tags
rubrics_metrics.description: Why you should never use \mbox within Wikipedia — the page's central exhortation: do not use \mbox as a substitute for \text or \mathrm inside math tags on Wikipedia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical context: \mbox was used as a workaround when \text and \mathrm were unavailable. The more important reason is that using \mbox on Wikipedia misleads people about the correct use of \mbox in normal LaTeX documents. Recommendation: remove or replace \mbox usages in Wikipedia math with appropriate alternatives such as \text or \mathrm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \text (or \mathrm) for text inside math
rubrics_metrics.description: The less important reason for avoiding \mbox is that it does not always yield the same results that \text or \mathrm yield. \text uses sizes appropriate to the particular context in which it is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the page: the subscript text using \mbox appears conspicuously bigger than when using \text. Therefore, when you want textual material in math mode, prefer \text{...} (or \mathrm where semantically appropriate) so that sizing and spacing are correct in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand \mbox's true purpose in (normal) LaTeX: preventing line-breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: \mbox's purpose in normal LaTeX is to prevent infelicitous line-breaks, not to force text-mode appearance. The page illustrates with prose: preventing a digit or expression from being left alone at the start of a new line (e.g., 'than 3' or 'than $x+y$').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: writing 'more \mbox{than 3}' keeps '3' from being orphaned on the next line; similarly 'more \mbox{than $x+y$}' will prevent a line-break between 'than' and the math expression. But this is how \mbox behaves in typesetting LaTeX — this line-break prevention behavior does not translate in the same way on Wikipedia/MathJax, so do not rely on \mbox for that purpose on Wikipedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not teach or propagate incorrect LaTeX practices via Wikipedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Using \mbox as a substitute for \text within Wikipedia math tags has misled many people about the intended purpose and behavior of \mbox when LaTeX is used in the normal way; Wikipedia's prior suggestion of \mbox caused users to adopt incorrect habits on other forums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid documenting or recommending workarounds that only work on Wikipedia. Prefer guidance that matches normal LaTeX semantics so readers learn correct practices transferable to standard LaTeX usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware rendering differences across browsers/MathJax/preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: The visual differences between \mbox and \text may not be visible in all environments: 'on some browsers, you might not see this effect if you're using MathJax, and on others you will, and it may also depend on how you have set your preferences.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test math rendering across common setups (different browsers and MathJax configurations) and prefer constructs (\text, \\mathrm) that produce consistent, context-appropriate results rather than relying on behavior that varies by renderer or user preferences.
